newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Two killed ahead of Zulu march - S.Africa police.
newsitem.headline: Two killed ahead of Zulu march - S.Africa police.

text.p: Two men were killed in Soweto township on Wednesday ahead of a march by Zulus to commemorate the deaths of more than 50 people in a demonstration three years ago, South African police said.
Around 10,000 people were expected to gather in Johannesburg's city centre for the commemoration, police spokesman Superintendent Govindsamy Mariemuthoo told Reuters.
Police had unrolled razor wire in front of the headquarters of Nelson Mandela's African National Congress (ANC) where eight Zulu demonstrators were killed by security guards during the 1994 march.

Police said trouble erupted early on Wednesday around Zulu workers' hostels in Soweto, the giant township southwest of the city as well as in some areas to the east of Johannesburg where roads were blocked.
Shots were fired at various hostels in Soweto and roads were barricaded with rocks.
"The situation is very tense in the area," Mariemuthoo said, adding that several commuter buses had been burnt.
There had also been reports of intimidation where people had been ordered to join the march, due to start around 0800 GMT.
The violence was believed to be linked to the demonstration, he said, adding that police had warned members of the public to stay away from the city centre on Wednesday.
